articleTitle: Management of a Mini Hydroelectric Plant According to an Annual Load Schedule of Public Lighting
abstract: Management of a mini hydroelectric power plant on a water main is considered so that the electricity production is coordinated with the current consumption of electricity for public lighting. Through a remote-control system, the parameters of the hydro unit are monitored, respectively the minimization of the difference production-consumption of electricity according to the set annual load schedule of the public lighting.

articleTitle: Autonomous DC Power Supply for Low-Power Consumers
abstract: A complete schematic diagram and results of an experimental study of an autonomous DC power supply for low-power consumers are presented. The main elements for its implementation are a photovoltaic panel, charge controller with Maximum Power Point Tracking, an ultracapacitor and a charge pump. A characteristic feature is a minimum amount of elements using to convert solar energy to DC voltage for the consumer, providing flexibility in choosing its value depending on the consumer's needs. Oscillograms from the experimental studies and results for the available stored energy and charging times at two values of the ultracapacitor - 10F and 100F - are shown.

articleTitle: Intelligent Management of Harmonic Distortions in the Electrical Network Caused by Modern LED Lighting Systems
abstract: As the use of LED lighting and other energy-efficient technologies increases, lighting-induced harmonics are becoming an increasingly significant problem for electrical systems. They are non-linear components in the electrical grid that generate additional electrical signals at frequencies that are multiples of the main grid frequency. These additional signals can lead to energy losses, overheating and disturbances in the electrical network. The purpose of this report is to present the importance of intelligently managing the harmonics induced by lighting systems and how the use of artificial intelligence can improve the quality of electrical energy in such systems. Intelligent lighting control systems use advanced algorithms and technologies that allow efficient control and reduction of the impact of harmonics in the electrical network. The use of artificial intelligence in these systems leads to more efficient use of electrical energy and a reduction in harm to electrical systems resulting from harmonics.

articleTitle: LTSpice Based Stability Analysis of DC-DC Converter for LED Drivers
abstract: This article presents a stability analysis of a boost DC-DC converter for powering an LED strip. A model of a DC converter is presented and the principle of operation is described. LTSpice software was used to implement the mathematical model. LED strip data provided by the manufacturer is used. Simulation results of the realized studies by Fourier transformation are presented. Investigating the influence of transient in LED drivers is useful in order to ensure the stability of the manufactured device under various external influences.

articleTitle: Possibilities of Obtaining Electricity from Biomass
abstract: Possibilities of generating electricity from biomass (as a renewable energy source - RES), are the object of the present study. The research is based on the biomass, which is typical for Bulgaria. It is mainly waste wood from wood processing enterprises and forestry farms. It has an inhomogeneous composition and comes from different sources. This makes it very difficult and almost impossible to analytically determine the main parameters of this type of fuel. Therefore, a passive experiment has been carried out for a certain lower calorific value of the fuel. This is the main parameter, determining the technology for waste wood use for energy needs. Analysis of the possibilities for producing electricity and heat from this energy carrier has been made on the basis of the obtained results. The advantages of using this type of renewable energy source have been presented.

articleTitle: Information System for Planning the Development of Electric Power Distribution Networks
abstract: The paper presents a developed information system for conducting short-term planning of the development of distribution networks with connected decentralized energy sources. The information system includes data on the configuration of the electric grid, the capacities of both the consumers and the decentralized energy sources for the short-term planning period; data on the throughput capacity of the power lines; technical and economic parameters, and others. The main blocks of the information system and its use in the process of short-term planning of distribution networks are described.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Impact of Snow Cover on Photovoltaic System
abstract: The current report presents a study on the impact of accumulated snow on the production of electrical energy from photovoltaic panels. In addition to the characteristics of the snow cover, factors such as solar radiation, humidity, air temperature, and the geographical orientation of the panels have been taken into account. The reported data cover a period during which the photovoltaic panels were partially or fully covered with snow. Data analysis shows that the influence of snow presence on photovoltaic panels should not be considered solely regarding the electric power generated by them, and there is no clear-cut relationship observed between the amount of snow and electricity generation.

articleTitle: Simulation-based Acquisition of Induction Motor Characteristics with Computed Parameters
abstract: The aim of this paper is to describe specific methods for using program models of an induction motor in the MATLAB/Simulink environment and their application as a supplement in engineering practice and the educational process as well as academic use in higher education institutions.

articleTitle: Harmonic Analysis of SEPIC DC-DC Converter
abstract: In the presented work, a harmonic analysis has been implemented to determine the resonance occurrence node of the Sepic DC-DC converter. The simulation studies were implemented in MATLAB/Simulink. Two cases of transistor conduction are presented. The differential equations for describing the processes in the converter are presented. State space matrices are used to implement harmonic analysis. Simulation studies are obtained and comments are made on the advantages and disadvantages of the methods used.

articleTitle: Spectral Power Distribution of Artificial Light Sources Leading to Alpha Opic Influence on Humans
abstract: The paper presents an investigation on the possibilities to introduce LED indoor luminaires, that are not only efficient but also have a significant impact on the natural cyclic processes in the human body. A combination of spectral power distributions of existing LEDs is made, so that composite spectra obtained positively influences the retinal cells in the human body and leads to increase in alertness and productivity. The alpha-opic influence of the new spectral power distributions is estimated, and based on the results some important conclusions are made. With the emergence of LEDs as most efficient light source and the tendency for replacement of all the existing sources of light with their LED alternatives comes the question whether this replacement leads only to reduction in the consumption of electrical energy for lighting or also has other advantages, connected to the influence of the solid state lighting on the human body. In the natural evolution of life, human beings are used to daylight and have been using it until now as a free and very powerful light source. The illuminance levels in the open on an average sunny day in Bulgaria exceed 100000 lux and go under 1000 lux at cloudy skies, which levels are significantly higher, than those reached in indoor spaces [1]. Nevertheless, what the weather is, however, during the day there is always daylight and this daylight influences and dictates the cyclic processes in the human body. Nowadays, because of the great variety of artificial light sources that exist, light is available all the time. And here arises the question whether the illuminance levels, prescribed by the standard for lighting of indoor workplaces EN 12464-1 [2] that are significantly lower than those in the open can influence the circadian rhythms and if yes to what extent, compared to the natural daylight. The lower illuminance levels indoors are not the only consideration, taken into account when such an estimation is made. The more important question is whether the spectral power distribution of the artificial light sources, that is completely different from that of the daylight and depend on the principle of light generation, can lead to stimulation of the retinal cells and lead to realization of the non-visual effects of light, the way that it leads to vision. A lot of research is carried out on these topics nowadays, but a straightforward decision is yet to be reached. And the most important questions to be answered are two. The first is whether the light levels indoors are enough to make the central master clock, which in humans is the suprachiasmatic nuclei (SCN) operate the same way as it does when it is submitted to daylight. Although the light, emitted by all the artificial light sources used for general lighting is visually intercepted as “white” in the retina of the eye, their chronobiological influence on circadian rhythms is not equal and its influence on hormones’ secretion and the human psychology differs to a great extent. So, the second important question is whether artificial light spectral power distribution with non-visual influence close to that of the natural light can be reached. Until recently, it was considered that rods and cones are the photoreceptors convicting the visual process and the retinal ganglion cells with their photopigment melanopsin are responsible for the circadian rhythms, alertness, and melatonin suppression. The most recent research findings, however, forward new evidence that these ganglion cells (the so-called photosensitive retinal ganglion cells) also contribute to visual perception modulation and the cones influence to a sudden extend the non-visual effects of light and the length of the exposure to light [3].

Author Keywords: circadian efficiency of spectral power distributions

articleTitle: LED Retrofitting for Fluorescent Troffers with Minimum Enviromental Impact – Case Study
abstract: The paper presents a case study on the possibilities for direct use of luminaire housing and optical system of fluorescent troffers for development of new LED luminaires. The use of existing materials and minimum addition of components will not only lead to energy savings but will also contribute to a great extent to cost savings and will increase the sustainability of lighting systems. The idea here is to use LED elements, not retrofit lamps, which gives greater flexibility and opportunity for modelling of the light distribution of the new fixtures.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Operation of a Mini Hydroelectric Plant for the Needs of Street Lighting
abstract: The pumping stations of the main water pipelines for the settlements provide the possibility of operation as a mini hydroelectric power plant (HEPP) when water consumption is low. Thus, part of the kinetic energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{1}}{}^{\mathbf{2}}-\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{2}}{}^{\mathbf{2}})/\mathbf{2}$</tex> of the water supplied to the buffer tank is utilized, and the produced electricity is provided to the Municipality for the needs of street lighting. When large quantities of water are delivered during the day, the hydro unit works as a pumping station, with electricity supplied by the municipal PV power plant.

articleTitle: Approaches for Implementing Artificial Intelligence in Cyber-security to Improve, Speed up and Optimize Processes
abstract: This paper provides an examination of how Artificial intelligence applies in cyber security's difficult job of preventing and guarding information. Dealing with broad attack surface, big number of applications and large number of users makes the defended territory too vast to deal with [1]. All of this creates challenges for cyber security with the large amounts of data to be analyzed and understood. Traditional security methods are not enough to stop cybercriminals from breaching data and inflicting damage. Artificial Intelligence, with machine learning algorithms, continuous learning mechanisms and real-time data processing, offers fundamental tools to cybersecurity to use and enhance approaches to recognize network intrusions, data breaches, phishing and spam emails, malware attacks, and to alert security vulnerability when appears.

articleTitle: Power Supply for Fast Charging Stations for Electric Vehicles Positioned on the Trakia Motorway in Bulgaria Through an Off-Grid Photovoltaic Plant with Storage System
abstract: Electric vehicles have an important role in reducing greenhouse gas emissions. In order to replace diesel vehicles with electric ones, fast charging stations for electric vehicles need to be installed throughout the country's road network. This in turn could be a cumbersome process and lead to problems in the electrical power system. In order to avoid this, for powering the electric vehicle charging stations, it is appropriate to use an off-grid PV plant with a storage system.

articleTitle: Implementation and Study of a PMSM Drive with Sensorless Field-Oriented Control for a Fan Application
abstract: The paper presents an application of sensorless field-oriented control of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) for a high-efficiency electrical drive of industrial fans. Generally, the application requires high efficiency due to the continuous operation of ventilation systems. The replacement of the traditionally used induction motors with permanent magnet synchronous motors and an electronic converter aims to reduce electricity costs for ventilation in industrial enterprises in the long term.

articleTitle: Public-private Partnership between a Municipality and a Water Supply Company in the Field of Street Lighting
abstract: the report examines the possibility of a public-private partnership between the Municipality and the Water Supply Company (WSC). During the hours of the day, with maximum water consumption, the hydro unit works in “motor-pump” mode, and using electricity from the PV power plant. With low water consumption at night, the mode is “turbine-generator”, providing the generated electricity for the needs of street lighting.

articleTitle: Options for Power Supplying an Object by Medium or High Voltage
abstract: The paper proposes an assessment of the possibility of supplying electricity to a mining and flotation plant and a mine near the village of Rozino at a set installed capacity of 10 MVA. Medium or high voltage power supply options are considered. The necessary investments for construction of the two types of power lines are approximately close in value and do not have a significant impact on the choice of a supplying voltage. Small savings can be realized in the short term, but in the long run it is indicative that a 110 kV power supply should be chosen. The provided data and the calculated values are obtained with the average consumption of electricity set by the Contracting Authority. The obtained results are analyzed and conclusions are drawn, useful for the operation of electricity distribution networks.

Author Keywords: investments for construction of power lines

articleTitle: Choosing a Strategy for Time-limited Designing of Power Distribution Grids With Consideration of Mode Constraints
abstract: A methodology for time-limited designing of medium voltage power grids with joined sources of renewable energy is discussed in this publication, considering limitations of mode nature. The methodology comprises the following chosen criteria: Minimum costs; minimal power losses, and minimum amount of undelivered electricity. The developed strategies contain different options for building decentralized energy sources and comparing their power with the load power in the connected branch. Different scenarios are considered for each strategy. Calculations are performed for each strategy and each scenario, taking into account the stages of introducing the decentralized energy sources into the connected branch. The limitations of mode nature in the methodology concern the permissible magnitudes of the currents in the branches, the values of the voltages in the nodes and the deteriorated quality indicators of the electricity, produced by the decentralized energy sources. Results from the implementation of the methodology for short-term planning of medium voltage distribution networks with connected decentralized energy sources are analyzed.

articleTitle: Lighting Mesurements of Recostructed Multifunctional Sports Hall
abstract: The main goal of the renovated artificial lighting system is to increase energy efficiency and reduce energy costs through technological renewal and modernization. The aim is to create conditions for holding competitions and events of the highest rank (European, world championships), as well as ensuring the coverage of these events through live television broadcasts in high definition. Measurements of the lighting system were carried out in order to establish whether the standard requirements are met.

articleTitle: Development Trends in Hydrogen Power Engineering
abstract: The paper considers the main trends and problems in the development of the hydrogen power engineering. The advantages and disadvantages of hydrogen, the main problems of hydrogen energy, the possibility of creating a global hydrogen market are presented. The first steps in the use of hydrogen in large-scale power generation are described. The prospects for the development of the hydrogen power engineering are analyzed. Conclusions are drawn about the future of hydrogen energetics.

articleTitle: The Impact of Adaptive Lighting on Psychophysical State in Educational Environments — An Experimental Study
abstract: The study presents practical results for the influence of dynamic adaptive lighting and environmental features on the psychophysical state of participants in university educational process. The results are obtained by conducting tests under precisely controlled indoor lighting conditions, various performed activities, different positions of the participants as well as the viewing perspectives. Analyses of the psychological comfort, mood, cognitive performance, and physical state of the objects of the study were made.

articleTitle: Research and Analysis of the Hourly Variation of Solar Radiation at the Photovoltaic Power Plants in Gabrovo Tech Park
abstract: The paper presents research on the hourly variation of solar radiation at the photovoltaic power plants in Gabrovo Tech Park. Monitoring system measurements of solar radiation data for 2021 are processed. The data for hourly variation of solar radiation are presented graphically as individual points for each hour of the day in figures for different months, with the corre3sponding trends of the change in the average values of solar radiation for the given hour of the day, and the change in the maximum recorded values for the hour. A regression analysis of the data for the hourly variation of the solar irradiation was performed, and for every month are obtained polynomials of the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-degree, with coefficients of determination <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}} >\quad \mathbf{0.96}$</tex>. Analyses and conclusions on the research are made.

articleTitle: Complex Assessment of the Efficiency of the Neutral Grounding Modes in the Distribution Networks
abstract: The paper proposes an assessment of the efficiency of different ways of grounding the neutral in distribution networks by introducing a generalized indicator. The three ways of grounding the neutral in distribution networks have been considered: isolated neutral; grounded through an arc suppression reactor and grounded through an active resistance. Three factors, influencing on the efficiency of the neutral grounding have been chosen: continuity of the electricity supply to the consumers; current magnitude of a single phase-to-ground fault; multiplicity of maximum overvoltages. The assessment of the most influencing factor on the generalized performance indicator for the different ways of grounding the neutral has been made by applying the mathematical game theory. The obtained results have been analyzed and conclusions, useful for the operation of distribution electrical networks, have been drawn.

articleTitle: Effects of Sliding-Mode Observer Parameters and Current Controllers' Setup in a Sensorless PMSM Drive
abstract: The work presented in the paper deals with a study of the influence of the parameters necessary for tuning a sensorless field-oriented control of a permanent mag-net synchronous motor (PMSM) - control without a speed sensor mounted on the motor shaft. A sliding-mode observer is implemented, considering not only the effects of motor parameters on the observer for rotor angular position and speed but also the influence and methods for tuning the current and speed controllers

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of the Lighting Engineering Characteristics of an Indoor LED Luminaire with different Microprism Lenses
abstract: Measurement results and analysis of photometric characteristics and efficacy of indoor LED luminaire, constructed with multi-variate of the optical system - without and with different microprism lens samples, are presented in this paper. By using a goniophotometer the results for the measured light distribution, luminous intensity, beam angle, average luminance at vertical angular zones, output luminous flux and total luminous efficacy for the different microprism lenses samples of the indoor LED luminaire are presented. The efficiency loss in the optical system with different microprism lenses is shown. Comparative lighting calculations of the study indoor LED luminaire without and with different microprism lenses are done.

articleTitle: Elastic Analysis for Homogeneously Graded Rotating Disks with Linearly-Varying Thicknesses
abstract: This study presents the elastic stress analysis of a high-speed rotating disks made of homogeneously graded material with linear-variable thickness. The radial and tangential stress distributions and displacements of the rotating disks are investigated for linearly varying thicknesses in the radial direction by means of different slope of the line that forms the profile of the disk. The main goal of this research is to study the effect of mechanical load on the strength of the disk with linear-varying profile by using analytical solution and finite element method. The inner and outer surfaces of rotating disk are subjected to different pressures simultaneously. To verify the reliability of the results, the appropriate comparisons with the exact analytical solution for homogeneous graded disk with uniform thickness are made at the same angular velocity and boundary loads. Finally, the lowest radial stress and a uniform distribution of tangential stress along the radius of the rotating disc for the corresponding line inclination are obtained.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Sports Lighting of Football Stadium
abstract: The main goal of sports lighting is to provide sufficient horizontal and vertical illumination for the playing field. To achieve this, we reviewed existing standards and requirements such as “BDS EN 12193:2019 Light and lighting. Lighting of sports facilities,” as well as those set by Union of European Football Assotiasions and Bulgarian Football Union. Additionally, we examined the control mechanisms governing the design of sports lighting systems, which play a crucial role in the overall process. Furthermore, we considered the procedure for measuring illuminance, including measurement points and methodologies outlined in standardized documents.

articleTitle: Renovation of Adaptive Tunnel Lighting with Lighting Cost Optimization
abstract: In the commonly encountered tunnels up to 500 m, the main lighting costs are determined by the daytime adaptation lighting. With an annual usability for Bulgaria of 4600 hours per year, the payment of funds for the rehabilitation of this type of equipment is determined by the purchase price of the illuminators and the costs of electricity and maintenance. The latter are relatively permanent, as modern LED lights last almost 10 years, after which they are replaced with more energy-efficient ones. Therefore, when replacing outdated lighting fixtures, a reasonable period for recovering the investment for the rehabilitation of this type of equipment is up to 5 years. The invested funds are recovered at the expense of lower electricity costs and easier maintenance, which is achieved by: 1) providing CLO (Constant Light Output) - reducing the intensity of light (dimming) of light sources (LS) in depending on their aging, avoiding energy overspending due to the MF=0.67 (Maintenance Factor) adopted in the design; 2) dimming of LS in the hours with reduced traffic, according to the conditions for safe traffic. Both ways do not require expensive technical facilities, which is why comparing expensive luminaires with high energy efficiency and cheaper ones with lower energy efficiency is not always in favor of the former. The report examines this aspect of an opportunity to rehabilitate daylight tunnel lighting for a tunnel in Bulgaria.

articleTitle: Red Bricks and White Collars: Exploring the Visual Comfort Dynamics of Exposed Brick Interiors in Office Environments
abstract: Contemporary office design faces a dynamic intersection of aesthetics and functionality, with exposed brick interiors gaining prominence for their unique visual appeal. However, a critical gap exists in understanding how daylight interacts with these architectural elements, particularly visual comfort. This research delves into the intricate interplay between daylight and exposed brick interiors in contemporary office design, emphasizing the essential balance between aesthetics and functionality. This study fills a crucial gap in current understanding. Employing a meticulous mixed-methods approach, three case studies from Kerala were selected to investigate daylighting dynamics within exposed brickwork interiors comprehensively. Live lux measurements formed the quantitative backbone, consistently revealing deficient lighting levels below recommended standards for office workspaces. Qualitative insights from occupant surveys added depth, capturing user perspectives on visual comfort. The study recognized the intrinsic link between architectural design and human experience, highlighting the importance of creating spaces conducive to well-being. Utilizing Autodesk Insight 2024, daylight simulations validated against real-time measurements provided crucial insights. Comparative scenarios, including plastered walls and increased window-to-wall ratio, showcased improvements in workspace illuminance, suggesting potential energy optimization strategies. Overall, this research offers valuable contributions to the discourse on crafting visually comfortable, sustainable, and aesthetically pleasing office environments. It underscores the necessity for thoughtful design interventions, acknowledging the delicate balance between architectural aesthetics and functional considerations in optimizing workplace design.

articleTitle: Study of the Spectral Characteristics of LED Domestic Lamps During the Warm-Up Process
abstract: The paper presents results of measured spectral characteristics of contemporary LED domestic lamps with different colour characteristics during the warm-up process to steady state. The measurements of the spectral characteristics of LED lamps are performed using a CCD spectroradiometer with an integrating sphere system and thermal camera. The measured relative spectral distribution of radiant flux in a turning on and a steady state of the LED lamps is presented comparatively. Measured and calculated peak wavelength in the region of the blue LED radiation, the relative change of the correlated colour temperature and colour rendering index during warm-up to a steady state of the tested LED lamps are presented. Conclusions regarding the measured and calculated spectral indicators of the tested LED domestic lamps are made.

articleTitle: Sustainable Energy Management & its Correlation with Renewable Resources
abstract: Energy management is part of energy sector since energy generation while Renewable energy sector has experienced a dramatic transformation over the 21th century which is driven by global commitments to tackle and reduce environmental impacts due to fossil fuels and foster a future which is more sustainable. Neither renewable resources and nor energy management never got maximized with serious principles and methods. Sustainability issues in terms of energy management is one of the open challenges which needs integrative sustainable framework and requires urgent solutions. Therefore, there is need for conclusive concept which could help both renewable resources and energy magnement practices to reach its pick. A research is brought through this paper with concept of sustainable energy management, principles and requirements, role in different aspects, importance, its correlation with renewables, methods applicable in smart grids and acknowledgment regarding sustainable energy management.

articleTitle: Increasing the Efficiency of Lighting Systems as an Element of City Power Supply Systems
abstract: The work is devoted to increasing the efficiency of the power supply and lighting systems of cities. The idea of the work is the automatic online control of modes of city lighting systems that consider the criteria of economic, ecological and social efficiency. The relevance of the research topic lies in the low efficiency of the power supply and lighting systems of cities because critically important criteria of social and environmental efficiency are not considered when evaluating parameters and modes. Neglecting them threatens the onset of severe social and environmental consequences. The purpose of the work is to increase the efficiency of the power supply and lighting systems of cities, based on the implementation of a system of operational control over the quality of lighting. To achieve the goal, the following main tasks were solved in the work: the regimes of the power supply and lighting systems of cities were evaluated; criteria for evaluating the effectiveness of their work are defined; criteria and scientific and technical solutions for increasing the efficiency of lighting systems as a component of power supply and city lighting systems are proposed.
